title: Mecpow Laser Engravers: X3S, X3 Pro, M1 and X5 Pro
metaDescription: Mecpow's laser engravers compared: the compact M1 5W, X3S 7W and 12W, X3 Pro 10W with air assist and the 33W X5 Pro with a 600x600 mm area, from $164.44 to $550.71.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: Mecpow has one of the largest laser ranges in the catalog, and it splits into three tiers: the small M1, the mid-size X3 family and the large X5 Pro. This guide compares five machines across them, from $164.44 to $550.71. Mecpow also sells many bundles with rotary rollers, beds, fume extractors and IR modules, which can make the same machine look like several different products, so read each listing's title for what is in the box.

items.label: M1 5W ($164.44)
items.value: 100x100 mm area, 0.01 mm accuracy, 10,000 mm/min, FDA Class 1, WiFi, USB and TF card

items.label: X3S 12W ($242.79)
items.value: 360x360 mm area, 0.06x0.08 mm precision, WiFi control, engraver and cutter

items.label: X3 Pro 10W + H44 bed ($264.86)
items.value: 10W with an air assist system and an H44 laser bed included

items.label: X5 Pro 33W ($550.71)
items.value: 600x600 mm area, 28,000 mm/min, auto air assist, safety lock, emergency stop, flame detection, offline engraving

pros: The M1 at $164.44 lists FDA Class 1 and a 0.01 mm accuracy figure, and it has WiFi, USB and TF card connections
The X3S 7W and 12W have a 360x360 mm area, much larger than the M1 for $23 to $78 more
The X3 Pro bundle includes air assist and an H44 bed for $264.86, so the two most useful accessories come in the box
The X5 Pro lists a safety lock, an emergency stop and flame detection, the most safety features of the five
The X5 Pro's 600x600 mm area and 28,000 mm/min speed are the largest and fastest here
cons: The M1's 100x100 mm area is small, so it suits tags and small items
The X3S listings do not mention air assist, so the X3 Pro is the better pick if you plan to cut
The X5 Pro costs $550.71, over three times the X3S 7W, and needs a large, ventilated workspace
Mecpow sells the same machines in many bundles, so a lower price may mean fewer accessories
Stated power and speed are best-case figures, and real results depend on material and settings

items.question: Which Mecpow should I buy first?
items.answer: For small engraving jobs, the M1. For a bigger bed at a low price, the X3S 7W, and the 12W if you want to cut. The X3 Pro bundle is the practical all-round pick because air assist and a bed are included.

items.question: What does FDA Class 1 mean for the M1?
items.answer: The listing states FDA Class 1. In general, Class 1 means the laser is safe under normal use because the beam is enclosed or limited. Check the listing and the manual for what that covers on this machine, and still follow the supplied safety guidance.

items.question: Is the X5 Pro worth the money?
items.answer: If you cut regularly or work on large pieces, yes: 33W, a 600x600 mm area and safety features such as flame detection and an emergency stop. For small engraving it is more machine than you need.

items.question: What are the M1 and X3 bundles?
items.answer: Mecpow lists the M1 with a rotary roller, a rotary chuck, a fume extractor, or a fume extractor plus a 1.2W IR module, and the X3S 12W with an R1 IR module. Prices differ, so compare what each bundle adds.

items.question: Do I need a fume extractor?
items.answer: For indoor work, smoke and fumes are a real issue, and ventilation or an extractor is advisable. Our guide "Laser Safety: Fire, Fumes and Eye Protection" covers it in more detail.

sections.content: Match the Mecpow tier to the work: the M1 for small marks, the X3S for a mid-size bed, the X3 Pro bundle for cutting with air assist and a bed included, and the X5 Pro for large, regular cutting. Check which accessories come in each bundle before you pay extra.
